ct-comp-2026-scanlon-sean.name: Sean Scanlon
ct-comp-2026-scanlon-sean.bio: Connecticut's 67th State Comptroller; former State Representative for the 98th District (2015-2023).

positions.stance: Running for re-election "to look out for taxpayers and make Connecticut more affordable for families, workers and small businesses."

ct-comp-2026-tooker-jennifer.name: Jennifer S. Tooker
ct-comp-2026-tooker-jennifer.bio: Former First Selectwoman of Westport and business executive with nearly 25 years in the international reinsurance industry.

positions.stance: Running for Comptroller "to restore accountability, transparency, and discipline to Connecticut's finances" as "an independent check and balance."
Believes "affordability starts with honest fiscal leadership: running government with the same discipline households and employers use every day."
Wants access to great schools for every student, believing "your zip code should not determine your opportunities in life."

ct-ag-2026-tong-william.name: William Tong
ct-ag-2026-tong-william.bio: Connecticut Attorney General, serving his second term.

ct-ag-2026-bolton-john.name: John Bolton
ct-ag-2026-bolton-john.bio: Connecticut attorney and former Westport Planning & Zoning Commissioner.

positions.stance: Will challenge policies that drive up utility costs, hold utilities accountable for unreasonable rate increases, and advocate for ratepayers before state regulators.
Will hold neighboring states accountable when their pollution or policies harm Connecticut's waters, taxpayers, or businesses.
Will aggressively enforce consumer protection laws, investigate AI-driven pricing, crack down on fraud, and protect seniors from scams.
Will enforce the Connecticut False Claims Act against contractors who defraud taxpayers and increase oversight of state spending.
Will use antitrust and consumer laws to scrutinize hospital mergers, challenge private equity takeovers, and enforce surprise-billing protections.

ia-sos-2026-pate-paul.name: Paul D. Pate
ia-sos-2026-pate-paul.bio: Small business leader serving his third term as Iowa Secretary of State.

positions.stance: Campaigns on making voting "Easy to Vote, Hard to Cheat," citing Voter ID and online voter registration.
"Clearing the red tape will help job creators do what they do best – grow Iowa's economy."
Stands with members of the armed services and backs programs making it easier for active-duty military to vote back home.

ia-sos-2026-peterman-ryan.name: Ryan Peterman
ia-sos-2026-peterman-ryan.bio: Former Naval Aviator, Senate Defense Fellow, and mentor at the U.S. Naval Academy.

positions.stance: Will protect Iowans' personal information, fight illegal requests for it, and collect and keep only the information the office needs.
Will make transparency "the default," publishing election guidance online in plain language and improving public-records responses.
Will visit each of Iowa's 99 counties during his term and hold regular public meetings and listening sessions.
Will meet regularly with county auditors, provide consistent timely guidance, and consult local officials before major administrative changes.
Will set response standards for calls, filings, and inquiries, simplify forms, and publish basic performance measures.

ia-aud-2026-cournoyer-chris.name: Chris Cournoyer
ia-aud-2026-cournoyer-chris.bio: Lieutenant Governor of Iowa and former State Senator, with over 27 years in the private technology sector.

positions.stance: "Iowa deserves a true taxpayer watchdog — not a political activist."
Says the Auditor's Office should implement innovative tools like AI and work with local governments to find efficiencies.
Wants to give citizens more transparency through enhanced promotion of Iowa's transparency portal.
Will make the Auditor's Office "a home for recommendations emerging from the Governor's DOGE Task Force on modernizing government operations."

ia-aud-2026-wettach-taylor.name: Taylor Wettach
ia-aud-2026-wettach-taylor.bio: Attorney who worked as a trade and national security lawyer and in the federal government.

positions.stance: Will "protect taxpayers by rooting out waste, fraud, and abuse, and ensure they know where their money is going."
Will fight corruption and stand up to politicians who want to weaken the authority of the State Auditor.
Will "defend the independence of the State Auditor's office – no matter who's in power."
Will work with anyone – Republican, Democrat, or Independent – "who believes accountability matters."

ia-treas-2026-smith-roby.name: Roby Smith
ia-treas-2026-smith-roby.bio: Iowa State Treasurer; former family banker, small business owner, and Iowa State Senator.

positions.stance: Pledges to "show up every day ready to work for Iowa's taxpayers" in the Treasurer's office.
Will oppose federal measures he calls unconstitutional surveillance and "protect the financial privacy of working Iowa families."
Will work to improve financial literacy education so every high school student graduates with money-management life skills.
Will continue raising awareness of the 529 College Savings Plan so more families use it.
Will raise awareness of the IABLE disability savings program and seek the best returns for its participants.

ia-treas-2026-norwood-john.name: John Norwood
ia-treas-2026-norwood-john.bio: Finance professional and Business Advisor with the Goldman Sachs 10,000 Small Businesses Program; former Soil & Water Conservation Commissioner.

positions.stance: Will work with the legislature and governor to save money, eliminate wasteful spending, and show Iowans how their taxes are spent.
Calls protecting IPERS his "#1 priority" and will oppose any attempts to privatize or weaken public employees' pension benefits.
Will ensure the ISave 529 program is not misused or mismanaged and improve it so families of all incomes can participate.

ia-ag-sec-2026-naig-mike.name: Mike Naig
ia-ag-sec-2026-naig-mike.bio: Iowa Secretary of Agriculture who has spent his career working in agriculture.

positions.stance: Working to expand international trade, strengthen domestic demand for Iowa products including biofuels, and grow local food systems like Choose Iowa.
Backs a "farmer-first, solutions-driven approach" expanding cover crops, buffers, and wetlands, without higher taxes and government mandates.
Committed to a safe food supply, protecting livestock from disease, and stronger oversight of pet breeders.
Focused on supporting beginning farmers and strengthening rural communities with jobs, education, health care, and child care.
Supports "conservative budgeting, lower taxes, and responsible government."

ia-ag-sec-2026-jones-chris.name: Chris Jones
ia-ag-sec-2026-jones-chris.bio: Research scientist and author who managed the Des Moines Water Works testing laboratory and worked as a University of Iowa research engineer.

positions.stance: Calls for "a more diverse rural landscape" with more kinds of crops and broader land ownership, since corn and soy cover 70% of land.
Supports taxpayer-funded off-ramps for farmers moving to sustainable practices, and enforceable pollution rules for those who don't.
Calls for "a strategic retreat from growing corn for fuel ethanol," returning much of that land to pasture.
Wants less pollution, more places to enjoy nature, and stronger local food systems connecting Iowa farms to Iowa tables.
Says pollution from the "corn-soybean-CAFO-ethanol production system must be regulated."

ia-ag-2026-bird-brenna.name: Brenna Bird
ia-ag-2026-bird-brenna.bio: Iowa Attorney General; former Guthrie County Attorney and counsel to Governor Terry Branstad.

ia-ag-2026-willems-nate.name: Nate Willems
ia-ag-2026-willems-nate.bio: Iowa labor attorney who has represented workers for nearly 20 years.

positions.stance: Will go after "wage theft, misclassification, and unpaid overtime so Iowans keep what they earn."
Will hold "corporations accountable when they break the law and cheat Iowa families."
Supports "holding criminals accountable, supporting our first responders, and helping victims."
Says the office shouldn't prioritize "personal political fights and national issues that have nothing to do with Iowans."
Will stop scams, enforce nursing home safety standards, and work with prosecutors to prevent fraud against seniors.

nv-sos-2026-aguilar-francisco.name: Francisco "Cisco" Aguilar
nv-sos-2026-aguilar-francisco.bio: Nevada Secretary of State; former General Counsel for Agassi Graf and founder of Blueprint Sports.

positions.stance: Prioritizes updating Nevada's business systems to reduce wait times and outages so businesses can focus on customers, not compliance.
Working so Nevada businesses can adjust business license fees in response to market conditions.
Strengthening election integrity by prioritizing cybersecurity and advocating for election workers.
Recruiting a new generation of poll workers and boosting turnout among Native American communities and young voters.

nv-sos-2026-marchant-jim.name: Jim Marchant
nv-sos-2026-marchant-jim.bio: Former Nevada Assemblyman and founder and CEO of technology and internet companies.

positions.stance: Supports "Strong Voter ID — Including Proof of U.S. Citizenship."
Supports "Paper Ballots — No Electronic Voting Machines" and precinct-level voting with hand counting.
Supports ending universal mail-in ballots and re-registering all voters to clean voter rolls.
Will advocate to repeal the Commerce Tax.
Will lower business registration costs, streamline corporate filings, and restore Nevada as a top incorporation destination.

nv-treas-2026-johnson-drew.name: Drew Johnson
nv-treas-2026-johnson-drew.bio: Government-spending watchdog who founded a Tennessee free-market think tank.

positions.stance: Will root out waste, reduce hidden fees, and review state accounts and vendor contracts so government lives within its means.
Will expand financial education to protect seniors from scams and help young Nevadans avoid debt.
Will modernize outdated state financial systems to cut errors and administrative costs.
Will strengthen Nevada's credit rating through disciplined fiscal management and protected reserves to lower borrowing costs.
Will refinance state bonds when interest rates fall to free up money for taxpayers.

nv-treas-2026-mathis-coleman-tya.name: Tya Mathis-Coleman
nv-treas-2026-mathis-coleman-tya.bio: Deputy Treasurer of Nevada leading the College Savings Division; UNLV faculty.

positions.stance: Will "safeguard state funds with responsible investment strategies and strong oversight."
Will "ensure clear reporting, accessible data, and honest communication about how your tax dollars are managed."
Will strengthen college savings programs "so every family, regardless of income or background, can plan for higher education."
Will "use evidence-based strategies that grow Nevada's resources while minimizing risk."
Will make financial decisions reflecting Nevada families' needs, "not special interests."

nv-ctrl-2026-macdougall-michael.name: Michael MacDougall
nv-ctrl-2026-macdougall-michael.bio: High school social studies teacher at the Adelson School in Southern Nevada.

positions.stance: Will work from day one to bring the state's annual financial report into full compliance with policy and law.
Will use the Controller's seat on the State Board of Transportation to improve access to public transportation in every county.
Will work to reduce Nevada's more than $900 million in uncollected tax revenue.

nv-ctrl-2026-matthews-andy.name: Andy Matthews
nv-ctrl-2026-matthews-andy.bio: Nevada State Controller since 2023; former Assemblyman and former President of the Nevada Policy Research Institute.

positions.stance: Will reintroduce legislation creating a Nevada Office of Inspector General to conduct independent audits of entities receiving state funds.
Will keep working with counties, cities and school districts to give the public better access to local-government spending data.
Will build on recent reforms so state auditing and financial reports provide data more quickly and efficiently.
Will "continue to fight for fiscal sanity in our state capital."

nv-ag-2026-cannizzaro-nicole.name: Nicole Jeanette Cannizzaro
nv-ag-2026-cannizzaro-nicole.bio: Prosecutor and Majority Leader of the Nevada State Senate.

positions.stance: Will support law enforcement against drug and human trafficking, get ghost guns off the streets, protect kids online, and crack down on scammers.
Will use every tool to protect abortion rights, birth control, and IVF, and protect women and doctors from prosecution.
Will go after corporations raising costs, enforce wage and benefits laws, fight wage theft, and target fraudsters targeting seniors.
Will fight back if the federal government cuts Nevadans' health care or education funding or makes Nevada a nuclear waste site.
Will protect Nevada's clean energy economy, take on corporate polluters, and protect access to public lands.

nv-ag-2026-guzman-fralick-adriana.name: Adriana Guzmán Fralick
nv-ag-2026-guzman-fralick-adriana.bio: Chairwoman of the Nevada Cannabis Compliance Board; former Carson City Chief Deputy District Attorney and General Counsel to Governor Jim Gibbons.

positions.stance: Will work to roll back provisions of 2019's AB 236 and restore strong sentencing for violent criminals, drug traffickers, and repeat offenders.
Will give law enforcement resources to dismantle drug networks and strengthen prevention programs to keep drugs out of schools.
Will ensure police and sheriffs have the resources, training, and legal backing they need.
Will prioritize protecting victims through stronger enforcement of restraining orders and swift prosecution of abusers.
Will work with law enforcement, educators, and parents to strengthen school security and coordinate responses to threats.

ar-sos-2026-hammer-kim.name: Kim Hammer
ar-sos-2026-hammer-kim.bio: Arkansas State Senator for District 16 since 2018; former eight-year member of the Arkansas House.

positions.stance: Will implement election laws passed by the Legislature and executive orders from the governor or president, keeping Arkansas "the most secure place to vote."
Believes Arkansans should be able to place issues on the ballot, but "changing our Constitution should not be easy."

ar-sos-2026-grappe-kelly.name: Kelly Grappe
ar-sos-2026-grappe-kelly.bio: Former Alltel and Verizon manager of nearly 25 years who runs a small business and farm.

positions.stance: Her top priority is restoring trust in elections by showing Arkansans how voting machines, testing, and verification work.
Will protect citizens' initiative and referendum power with clear checkpoints so petitions aren't lost on technicalities.
Will support all 75 counties by listening to county election officials and sharing practices that work.
Will improve FOIA tracking and proactively publish commonly requested public records online.

ar-ag-2026-griffin-tim.name: Tim Griffin
ar-ag-2026-griffin-tim.bio: Arkansas Attorney General and a colonel in the Arkansas Army National Guard.

ar-aud-2026-milligan-dennis.name: Dennis Milligan
ar-aud-2026-milligan-dennis.bio: Arkansas Auditor of State; former two-term Treasurer of State and Saline County Circuit Clerk.

positions.stance: Pledges to "always look for ways to serve our citizens more efficiently and cost effectively."

ar-lands-2026-jester-cole.name: Cole Jester
ar-lands-2026-jester-cole.bio: Arkansas Secretary of State and lawyer; former staff member to Governor Sarah Huckabee Sanders.

positions.stance: Pledges to shrink government while boosting efficiency.
Pledges to expand energy dominance through state leases.
Pledges to protect Arkansas's waterways and natural resources.
Pledges to investigate Chinese ownership near navigable waterways and state resources.

ks-sos-2026-day-jennifer.name: Jennifer Day
ks-sos-2026-day-jennifer.bio: Kansas State Representative for House District 48 with 16 years of business experience in technology, real estate, and finance.

positions.stance: Says voting should not be partisan and will work to "shut down disinformation" and ensure voters have the information they need.
Will keep voting systems "accurate, reliable, and free from political influence" and coordinate with county election officials.
Will study states with higher turnout and investigate implementing similar processes in Kansas.
Will expand programs to modernize and streamline business registration, making it easier to start and operate a business.

ks-sos-2026-proctor-pat.name: Pat Proctor
ks-sos-2026-proctor-pat.bio: Kansas State Representative and House Elections Committee chair; retired Army colonel, Wichita State assistant professor, and restaurant owner.

positions.stance: Will be "ever vigilant" against foreign and domestic threats to elections, working with law enforcement and state and federal partners.
Will "strongly safeguard Kansans' right to vote, ensuring every lawful vote counts and securing our ballots and election processes."
Says government should be "a helper, not a hindrance" and will prioritize making Kansas welcoming to business.
